day1_insight: A little recent rain (2.6 mm) may be carrying some runoff to the shoreline — a modest upward pressure on bacteria. The model's main signals right now: 2.6 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; elevated river/creek flow is raising risk by carrying watershed runoff to the shore; and high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach. The most recent sample, 5 days ago, was clean at 41 MPN/100mL.
day2_insight: Recent rain (21 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: 21 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; limited sunlight is raising risk (less UV to disinfect the water); and high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach. The most recent sample, 5 days ago, was excellent at 20 MPN/100mL.
day3_insight: Only a trace of rain has fallen recently (0.4 mm) — very little rain, and too little to drive meaningful runoff. The model's main signals right now: high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; limited sunlight is raising risk (less UV to disinfect the water); and seasonal pattern is raising risk — seasonal patterns (wet winters vs dry summers) set the baseline risk. The most recent sample, 4 days ago, was excellent at 20 MPN/100mL.
